results.text: The base station could not write the new binding into its binding table. A single occurrence can follow a power interruption during pairing; retry once after restarting the base station. If E-207 repeats, or the app lists a device that the base station table does not contain, the binding table is likely corrupted: escalate to FAE. Do not factory-reset the base station.

Escalate when any of the following holds: (1) two or more peripherals fail at the same time while the base station is online; (2) a firmware or protocol mismatch remains after an OTA attempt or OTA is not possible; (3) the standard frontline fix was executed and the problem persists; (4) the app's device list and the base station binding table disagree; (5) a device fails even next to the base station after a factory reset.

results.source: manual_base_station#Orphaned binding (device removed in app but still bound in base station)
results.text: If a device is removed in the app while it is offline or out of range, the base station may keep its entry. This orphaned ("ghost") binding still occupies a slot, so the base station can report E-201 although the app lists fewer devices than the limit. Frontline cannot clear it: the app only removes devices it lists, re-pairing does not free the slot, and a base-station factory reset is not allowed. Treat it as a binding-table inconsistency (app and base station disagree) and escalate to FAE, who remove the entry with the backend binding tool. Put the orphaned device id and the bound count (for example 8/8) in the ticket.

However, actionability is limited because no diagnostic questions were asked and no troubleshooting steps were performed, so the customer's account-sync hypothesis is never addressed. The response also presents detailed findings (E-207 logs, binding table mismatch, firmware/model) as established facts even though the session record shows no questions asked and no actions performed, meaning those checks are not supported by the record.
